Because remember, we wanted to understand the reason why in Wi-Fi we say every time we perform the backoff procedure for a given data packet, we roughly speaking double the contention window. So we increase it very significantly every time. Why do we do that? To reduce the probability of collision among contend nodes. Okay. So backoff is a probabilistic mechanism, and essentially Wi-Fi assumes that the reason why a transmitter is failing, failing, failing is because there are too many nodes in the network that try to access the channel to transmit a packet. The situation is too crowded. So what Wi-Fi says is, if you fail, fail, fail. Every time you fail means that there are other nodes trying, and you are selecting the same backoff, you have the same backoff time, and you keep colliding. So in order to reduce the probability of collision, each node needs to enlarge the possible values. So the choice right among the integers that can be selected. It's like when you have a bag with candies.
